tier1.text: Each abductor pollicis brevis moves the thumb away from the body. This movement, called abduction, swings the thumb forward to point straight out from the palm. This muscle belongs to the thenar muscles, which form the rounded bulge at the base of the thumb. Like the other thenar muscles, the abductor pollicis brevis starts and ends within the hand.

quotes.quote: The thenar muscles include the abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis, and the adductor pollicis. These muscles form the thenar eminence, the rounded contour of the base of the thumb, and all act on the thumb.

quotes.quote: They both originate and insert within the hand. The thenar muscles, which are located on the lateral part of the palm, are the abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis, and adductor pollicis.
